functions.description: Convert the beam span, uniform load intensity, modulus of elasticity and second moment of area to SI base units
inputs: the span length L of the simply supported beam with unit
the uniform load intensity w acting over the full span of the beam with unit
the modulus of elasticity E of the beam material with unit
the second moment of area I of the beam cross-section with unit
outputs: the uniform load intensity in newtons per metre
the modulus of elasticity in pascals
the second moment of area in metres to the fourth

functions.description: Compute the flexural rigidity EI from the modulus of elasticity in pascals and the second moment of area in metres to the fourth.
inputs: the modulus of elasticity in pascals
the second moment of area in metres to the fourth
outputs: the flexural rigidity EI in newton square metres

functions.description: Compute the maximum midspan deflection of a simply supported beam under a uniform load over its full span as 5wL^4 divided by 384EI.
inputs: the uniform load intensity in newtons per metre
the modulus of elasticity in pascals
the second moment of area in metres to the fourth
outputs: the maximum midspan deflection in metres

functions.description: Check the plausibility of a beam deflection by computing the span-to-deflection ratio and comparing it with the typical L/360 serviceability limit.
inputs: the maximum midspan deflection in metres
outputs: the plausibility judgement of the deflection

functions.description: Compute the maximum deflection in millimetres of a simply supported beam under a full-span uniform load from its span, load intensity, modulus of elasticity and second moment of area, reporting the location at midspan.
inputs: the span length L of the simply supported beam with unit
the uniform load intensity w acting over the full span of the beam with unit
the modulus of elasticity E of the beam material with unit
the second moment of area I of the beam cross-section with unit
outputs: the maximum deflection of the beam in millimetres with location at midspan

entry_points.text: A simply supported steel beam spans ●1 and carries a uniform load of ●2. With modulus of elasticity ●3 and second moment of area ●4, what is the maximum deflection?

params.description: the span length L of the simply supported beam with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive finite length with a length unit; physically meaningful spans are roughly 0.1 m to a few hundred metres. A zero or negative span is invalid.

params.description: the uniform load intensity w acting over the full span of the beam with unit
params.validity_range: Non-negative force per unit length with a force-per-length unit. Zero gives zero deflection; the linear-elastic formula holds only while the beam stays elastic and the load is within the design range.

params.description: the modulus of elasticity E of the beam material with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive stress unit value. Typical structural values are roughly 1 GPa to 500 GPa (steel about 200 GPa). Zero or negative is physically invalid.

params.description: the second moment of area I of the beam cross-section with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive length-to-the-fourth unit value. Realistic beam sections give roughly 10⁻⁸ m⁴ to 10⁻² m⁴. Zero or negative is invalid because the section must have area.

entry_points.text: A simply supported steel beam spans 6.0 m and carries a uniform load of 12 kN/m. With E = 200 GPa and I = 8.0 × 10⁻⁵ m⁴, what is the maximum deflection?
